# Writing clearly and concisely — Strunk's rules plus AI-writing anti-patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor — @softaworks' skill for agents that write prose humans will read (docs, commit messages, error messages, reports, UI copy). It pairs two halves: what to do — Strunk's Elements of Style compressed into 18 rules (active voice, positive form, definite specific concrete language, omit needless words, emphatic words at sentence end) with a reference-file index for loading just the needed section (~1k–4.5k tokens) when context is tight — and what not to do — the AI writing patterns to kill (puffery like "pivotal" and "enduring legacy", empty "-ing" phrases like "ensuring reliability", promotional adjectives like "seamless" and "cutting-edge", overused AI vocabulary like "delve" and "leverage", formatting overuse). It even includes a limited-context strategy: draft with judgment, then dispatch a subagent with the relevant section to copyedit. MIT-licensed. Honest caveats: style is taste-laden — Strunk's 1918 rules are a strong default but not a substitute for a project's own voice guide; the anti-pattern list is a moving target as model prose drifts; it guides prose quality, not factual accuracy. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
